messages:
maya: Heads-up — noticed a regression in TP all-reduce perf after the kernel-selector tweak yesterday. Small-message workloads (avg 1.2KB) drop throughput ~22%. Anyone else seeing this?

sanjay: seeing it on a couple of repros. latency tail jumps and utilization on comm streams spikes. suspect handshake/fragmenting behavior.

lee: repro command? I can run on the 8xA100 testbed.

maya: repro: `./run_tp_repro --tp=4 --batch=8 --seq=512 --profile=nccl --runs=50`

maya: attached perf-bot summary (ran on staging):
```
perf-bot: profile_id=pr-20260309-7
agg: allreduce_time +18% (median)
comm: ring stalls at 2.1ms handshake per pkt
kernel: autoswitch chose ring_kern_v2 for msg > 768B
msg_hist: 68% msgs in [256B,2KB]
kv_cache: hitrate stable, but kvcache flushes align with allreduce bursts
```

cassie: interesting — kernel selector rule uses msg_size threshold 768B. with our msg distribution the selector flips frequently mid-batch, causing mixed commshape and extra handshakes.

lee: profiler flame snippet (top 3):
```
1) nccl_ring_send (35%)
2) wait_for_handshake (22%)
3) compute_kv_flush (8%)
```

maya: note: when we force tree variant (`--force-collective=tree_small`) the stalls drop and throughput recovers ~14% vs regressed baseline.

sanjay: hypothesis: batching heuristics generate variable chunking so some tensors fall under selector threshold while coalesced neighbors go over it. That causes mixed reduction shapes and extra rendezvous. Also kvcache eviction during peak bursts amplifies IO and scheduling jitter.

cassie: quick mitigation options:
- bump selector threshold to 2KB for TP all-reduce
- enable homogeneous-kernel policy for TP partitions (force tree for <4k overall window)
- pad small tensors to 1.5KB at packing stage

maya: can we try a canary: change selector threshold -> 2048 and run nightly canary on perf cluster? If stable, rollout to dedicated pools.

lee: I'll run canary and post perf graphs. also adding a quick probe in kernel-selector to record per-batch msg size variance.

perf-bot: canary job scheduled: job=canary-tp-allreduce-3623, nodes=8xA100, schedule=ASAP

maya: thanks. also putting a note to eng-runtime runbook: watch kvcache flush alignment and handshake counts per-route.

sanjay: if canary looks good we should consider longer-term: selector should consider batch-level distribution (histogram) not per-tensor raw size. reduces flips and handshake overhead.

cassie: agreed. will prototype histogram-aware selector and a padding micro-optimizer.

maya: cool — keep thread updated with canary output. :thumbsup:
